title.en: Molecular trajectory import with topology-owned atom identity

summary: Bind trajectory coordinates to a fixed topology order and retain per-frame metadata before building molecular render meshes.
objective: Load a molecular trajectory and keep atom identity, selection and supplied connectivity stable through frame changes and render filtering.
intent_signals: Load a molecular trajectory and keep atom identity, selection and supplied connectivity stable through frame changes and render filtering.
example_prompts: Load a molecular trajectory and keep atom identity, selection and supplied connectivity stable through frame changes and render filtering.
applies_when: Bind trajectory coordinates to a fixed topology order and retain per-frame metadata before building molecular render meshes.

principles: The imported topology and its explicit coordinate-order mapping own atom identity. Mesh order, element color and distance-based guesses cannot substitute for that mapping.
Reading a trajectory is playback of supplied coordinates. It neither runs molecular dynamics nor proves that a bonded or interacting structure is scientifically correct.
implementation: Bind topology and trajectory revisions through a manifest with atom count, ordered atom keys and reader version. Validate a known mapping when available; matching counts alone do not prove coordinate order. Refuse an unidentified reorder rather than matching atoms by nearest positions.

Keep source atom indices separate from any filtered GPU buffer. Derive selection, bonds and residue metadata through a stable mapping; record whether attributes were read, guessed or absent. Configure guessing deliberately rather than accepting guessed masses/types as supplied facts.

A frame reader owns source frame index, available physical time, unit conversion and cell metadata. If time is absent use an explicitly labeled assumed interval or frame index; never infer physical time from playback FPS.

Copy a frame into immutable application state when retaining it across subsequent reads. A new topology or changed atom count starts a new mapping epoch; invalidate old selections and measurements before replacing meshes.
observable_checks: Use two topologies with the same atom count but a deliberately permuted identity mapping; reject the incompatible binding unless the permutation is supplied and applied consistently.
Select source atom 7, filter render atoms and seek backward then forward: atom 7 retains its identity and supplied bond endpoints.
Import a frame without time or bonds: report those fields absent/assumed according to policy, and never draw newly guessed bonds as source-provided connectivity.

known_limits: Fixed-topology trajectory scope only. Reactive trajectories, variable particle count and bond-changing chemistry require a different identity/event model.
Authored source-reviewed guidance only; no import adapter, runtime artifact or scientific pipeline was implemented or executed.
creative_affordances: Use a compact source-versus-display inspector to expose the specific transformation; layout and emphasis are authored choices, not validated usability findings.

claims.statement: MDAnalysis Universe requires trajectory coordinates to follow topology atom order; it also exposes optional topology guessing and current-step unit-cell dimensions.
claims.scope: MDAnalysis 2.10.0 documented import contract; no claim of automatic identity verification.

source_refs.locator: Universe class description; coordinates parameter; to_guess and force_guess; dimensions
